claims_about_writeup.why: contribution.md is indeed a description of the method (including its origin); calling it 'method description' is accurate, if minimal.

message_source_quote: A self-built stance direction alone (cos 0.97 with WBS) achieves 0.58 — it works but is essentially a reproduction.
writeup_source_quote: The starting point was White-Bear Steering (Raman et al. 2026), which shows that a stance direction from think/don't-think pairs over named concepts makes implied concepts readable through the plain J-lens.
rationale: Both documents identify the source as White-Bear Steering (Raman et al. 2026), the write-up spelling out the name and citation while the message uses the unmistakable acronym 'WBS' consistently (including tying it to the directed_modulation bank). Both say a self-built stance-only direction is essentially a reproduction of WBS (cos 0.97, pass@10 0.58), and both frame the method's novelty identically as the composite direction (cos 0.88 with WBS) that combines the stance contrast with an implication-elicitation contrast to raise pass@10 to 0.75, with the implication component alone being useless.
